report.summary: The only change makes /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts mode 0600. COPY leaves it owned by root, but the image runs as `USER tempo` (uid 1000), and pi, started by tempod through pi-acp, must read the file via `-e /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts`. pi can't load the Tempo extension, so the pi agent breaks or loses the tools allow/deny enforcement and per-session MCP registration that the spec says only this extension provides. The image test's R_OK check on this path would also fail. Revert to 0644.

findings.text: tempo-profile.ts is copied as root-owned 0600 while every process in the container runs as user tempo, so pi can't read or load the Tempo extension.

evidence.why: COPY without --chown makes the file root:root, and 0600 lets only root read it. Line 79 `USER tempo` runs tempod, and so pi-acp and pi, as uid 1000. The spec (01, pi wrapper) loads `-e /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts`, which now fails with EACCES. That disables the tool_call guard that enforces tools.allow/deny (the spec says the flags only hide tools) and the per-session MCP registration. packages/tempod/test/image.test.ts asserts `accessSync("/opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts", constants.R_OK)` as uid 1000, which would throw. `chmod 0755 /opt/tempo /opt/tempo/pi` covers only the folders.

findings.text: No spec or IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES change goes with this permission change. The file holds no secrets (it reads mcp.json and env when it runs), so making it private gives no security benefit.

checked.risk: Build and runtime environment: file mode, owner and the user that runs processes
Spec: pi extension loading and enforcement
Security: whether the file holds secrets that would justify 0600
Tests: whether any test covers file readability
